stages.title: Rivals: shared
stages.summary: Two species of swarm, A (blue) and B (orange), in one world, each with its own rule, mass and pheromones, sensing the other's. A cheese is eaten once their combined robots fill its ring, and each swarm owns the share of the ring it holds. Both swarms are paid for every cheese eaten, whoever eats it: the cooperative control, the same objective as Feast split across two species. Each swarm learns only from its own payoff and updates only its own rule. Scored on the share of the cheese value eaten within the time limit, each layout played twice with the nests swapped. Fog cap 0.45 for both swarms.

stages.title: Rivals: zero-sum
stages.summary: Two species of swarm, A (blue) and B (orange), in one world, each with its own rule, mass and pheromones, sensing the other's. A cheese is eaten once their combined robots fill its ring, and each swarm owns the share of the ring it holds. Each swarm is paid its share of every cheese minus the other's, so one swarm's gain is the other's loss: the competitive control. Each swarm learns only from its own payoff and updates only its own rule. Scored on the share of the cheese value eaten within the time limit, each layout played twice with the nests swapped. Fog cap 0.45 for both swarms.

stages.title: Rivals: stag hunt
stages.summary: Two species of swarm, A (blue) and B (orange), in one world, each with its own rule, mass and pheromones, sensing the other's. A cheese is eaten once their combined robots fill its ring, and each swarm owns the share of the ring it holds. Two small cheeses either swarm can eat alone (worth 1 each) and one big cheese, the stag (worth 4), whose ring needs more robots than either swarm has. Each swarm is paid its own share. Hunting the stag together pays more, but only if the other swarm comes too. Each swarm learns only from its own payoff and updates only its own rule. Scored on the share of the cheese value eaten within the time limit, each layout played twice with the nests swapped. Fog cap 0.45 for both swarms.

stages.title: Chase
stages.summary: One cheese on terrain that runs from the swarm: every 2 steps it moves one square toward the side with the least robot mass within 4 squares, blocked by walls and by squares holding half a robot or more. Eaten once its ring is full. A scripted swarm that can see the cheese catches it in 56 to 81% of layouts, so the task is fair; the blind swarm has to find it by touch and pin it. Training speeds the cheese up level by level (still, then every 16, 8, 4, 2 steps); val always uses full speed. The second run (slower curriculum, an earlier fog limit, credit for ground covered by solid robots) caught the full-speed cheese in up to 16/22/8% of val layouts with fog, but under the 0.45 fog cap only 5/3/6% (baseline 0/2/0%), and none at all once the swarm was fully compact. Not solved; the stage stays open.

stages.title: Feast
stages.summary: Two to four cheeses on terrain; each vanishes once its ring is full, and the swarm must eat them all. No smell, pheromones only. Trained from scratch, no curriculum. The loss is the task (unfilled rings, plus crowding because robots take up space), a cost per step until everything is eaten, credit for floor that solid robots have covered, and a limit on fog (see below) that starts wide open and tightens once the swarm can eat. A run only counts at val fog of 0.45 or less on every split, the level of the accepted terrain swarm. Closed as a weak proof of concept on the 352-minute checkpoint of v4-feast-explore2: test 0.846, eating everything in 48% of unseen sizes, 6% of bigger worlds and 27% of damaged swarms, at fog 0.36 to 0.39, against 0% for the hand-written baseline. Bigger worlds are the weak spot: the swarm cannot search them without spreading thin.

aside.title: The fog hack
aside.text: With the loss being the task alone, the swarm found a shortcut. Robot mass in the simulation is continuous, so a square can hold a few hundredths of a robot. The swarm dissolves into a thin film over the whole world, and the film thickens wherever it touches a cheese's ring until the ring is full. It never searches, because it is already everywhere. No swarm of whole robots could do this: the objective said 'fill every ring' and never said the swarm has to stay made of robots. It also outscores every fog-free swarm trained so far. Run v4-feast-ema at 60 minutes, on the same held-out layouts; fog is the share of the swarm sitting on squares with less than half a robot.

stages.title: Terrain, 6x time
stages.summary: v3a with the time limit doubled to 6 steps per grid square, trained from scratch. Closed as a proof of concept: test 0.695 (52/38/44% of layouts) against 0% for the hand-written baseline; blocking pheromones drops it to 0%. The main weakness is recruiting the whole swarm and holding the formation, not time: with 4x the time limit, val success rises only from 46/44% to 58/62%. Reuniting separate nests is also weak.

stages.title: Terrain
stages.summary: No smell, pheromones, the whole swarm must gather, and random cave-like walls covering up to 30% of the world. Time limit 3 steps per grid square. Best blind val 0.724 (44/39/42%); the scent-following control reached 96/95/89%.

stages.title: No smell
stages.summary: Touch only. Robots lay pheromones, only robots write them, and a scrap of a robot moves in proportion to its mass. Late in the stage, success also required the whole swarm to gather.

stages.title: Smell
stages.summary: Every square smells the cheese, so the environment hands each robot an arrow. Saturated near the physical limit; final test 0.267 vs baseline 0.405.
